script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 12. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

You're spinning through space at about 1,000 miles per hour right now.  You don't feel it because everything around you moves together.  This spin—one rotation every 24 hours—creates the most fundamental rhythm of human existence: day and night.

At the equator, Earth's surface moves at about 1,000 mph. You don't feel it because the atmosphere moves with you and there's nothing fixed to compare against. Motion is relative—and we're all in motion together. Dinosaurs experienced 23-hour days.  Tidal friction from the Moon gradually slows Earth's rotation.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Every sunset is a reminder that darkness is temporary.  Every sunrise proves that no matter how dark the night, light returns.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Circadian Awareness - Honor Your Rhythm.

Here's your activity: Track your energy today: when are you most alert? Most tired? Most creative? Your body has wisdom about timing. Try to schedule one important task during your peak energy period tomorrow. This helps you align activities with your natural energy cycles.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why we have day and night can be applied to circadian awareness - honor your rhythm. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
